cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.long_name: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction
cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.short_description: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction.
cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.long_description: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction. Prevalence rates are calculated by searching for certain diagnosis codes in Medicare beneficiaries’ claims. A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf

info.long_description: Percent of Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries with Schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders. Prevalence rates are calculated by searching for certain diagnosis codes in Medicare beneficiaries’ claims. A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf

epic_n_concussion.long_name: ED Encounters with a Concussion Diagnosis
epic_n_concussion.short_description: Monthly count of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis (ICD-10-CA S06.0).
epic_n_concussion.long_description: Monthly count of emergency department encounters with a concussion diagnosis, per Epic's "Concussion( ICD-10-CA: S06.0 )" ED Diagnoses grouping. Data from Epic Cosmos, which contains de-identified data from 300M+ patients across 1,600+ hospitals. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic and imputed as 5; see epic_n_concussion_suppressed_flag. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America - the denominator (epic_n_ed_encounters) is all ED encounters regardless of diagnosis. Stratified by age at time of visit and evaluated sex; age buckets are Epic's own (not the PopHIVE standard bands). As of the 2852165 export the buckets are contiguous (10-13 Years, 14-17 Years); an earlier export (session 2851311) used 10-12 Years and had a gap at age 13.

epic_pct_concussion.long_description: Monthly percentage of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis, computed as epic_n_concussion / epic_n_ed_encounters * 100 - a percent of all ED encounters, NOT a rate per 100,000. Where the numerator was suppressed it is imputed as 5 before the percentage is computed. Where the denominator was itself suppressed the percentage is left missing, because dividing by the imputed denominator of 5 would assert a meaningless value; those cells are marked by epic_n_ed_encounters_suppressed_flag. Data from Epic Cosmos SlicerDicer. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America.
epic_pct_concussion.name: epic_pct_concussion

Estimates are reported overall and stratified (separately) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade; grade is mapped to approximate modal ages (9th=14, 10th=15, 11th=16, 12th=17). Missing estimates are set to 0 and flagged: pct_current_marijuana_suppressed = 1 marks values CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample size), and pct_current_marijuana_not_asked = 1 marks geography-years in which the question was not asked. Note: New York state estimates exclude New York City.

info.short_description: Percent of high school students who had a concussion from playing a sport or being physically active.
info.long_description: Weighted percentage of U.S. high school students who had a concussion from playing a sport or being physically active, from the CDC Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) (topic: Physical Activity; YRBSS question code: H76). Estimates are reported overall and stratified (separately) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade; grade is mapped to approximate modal ages (9th=14, 10th=15, 11th=16, 12th=17). Missing estimates are set to 0 and flagged: pct_sports_concussion_suppressed = 1 marks values CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample size), and pct_sports_concussion_not_asked = 1 marks geography-years in which the question was not asked. Note: New York state estimates exclude New York City.

cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.long_name: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction
cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.short_description: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction.
cms_acute_myocardial_infarction.long_description: Prevalence among Medicare Fee for Service patients of Acute myocardial infarction. Prevalence rates are calculated by searching for certain diagnosis codes in Medicare beneficiaries’ claims. A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf

info.short_description: Percent of Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries with Chronic kidney disease.
info.long_description: Percent of Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries with Chronic kidney disease. Prevalence rates are calculated by searching for certain diagnosis codes in Medicare beneficiaries’ claims. A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf
info.statement: {value}% of Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries have Chronic kidney disease.

A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf

A beneficiary is considered to have a condition if the CMS administrative data has a claim indicating that the beneficiary is diagnosed for a specific condition over the reference time period (one, two, or three years, depending on the condition chosen) or, in the case of ESRD and disability, if the reason for entitlement (original or current) is listed as disabled or ESRD in the MBSF. The definitions used are the FFS definitions, based on ICD10 codes: https://www2.ccwdata.org/documents/10280/19139421/chr-chronic-condition-algorithms.pdf

epic_n_concussion.long_name: ED Encounters with a Concussion Diagnosis
epic_n_concussion.short_description: Monthly count of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis (ICD-10-CA S06.0).
epic_n_concussion.long_description: Monthly count of emergency department encounters with a concussion diagnosis, per Epic's "Concussion( ICD-10-CA: S06.0 )" ED Diagnoses grouping. Data from Epic Cosmos, which contains de-identified data from 300M+ patients across 1,600+ hospitals. Counts of 10 or fewer are suppressed by Epic and imputed as 5; see epic_n_concussion_suppressed_flag. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America - the denominator (epic_n_ed_encounters) is all ED encounters regardless of diagnosis. Stratified by age at time of visit and evaluated sex; age buckets are Epic's own (not the PopHIVE standard bands). As of the 2852165 export the buckets are contiguous (10-13 Years, 14-17 Years); an earlier export (session 2851311) used 10-12 Years and had a gap at age 13.
epic_n_concussion.name: epic_n_concussion

epic_pct_concussion.short_description: Monthly percent of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis (ICD-10-CA S06.0).
epic_pct_concussion.long_description: Monthly percentage of ED encounters with a concussion diagnosis, computed as epic_n_concussion / epic_n_ed_encounters * 100 - a percent of all ED encounters, NOT a rate per 100,000. Where the numerator was suppressed it is imputed as 5 before the percentage is computed. Where the denominator was itself suppressed the percentage is left missing, because dividing by the imputed denominator of 5 would assert a meaningless value; those cells are marked by epic_n_ed_encounters_suppressed_flag. Data from Epic Cosmos SlicerDicer. Population base per SlicerDicer session 2852165: data model ED Encounters, population base All ED Encounters, criteria Country of Residence = United States of America.

pct_alcohol_drugs_before_sex.long_name: YRBSS: Drank alcohol or used drugs before last sexual intercourse (Sexual Behaviors)
pct_alcohol_drugs_before_sex.short_description: Percent of high school students who drank alcohol or used drugs before last sexual intercourse.
pct_alcohol_drugs_before_sex.long_description: Weighted percentage of U.S. high school students who drank alcohol or used drugs before last sexual intercourse, from the CDC Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) (topic: Sexual Behaviors; YRBSS question code: H60). Estimates are reported overall and stratified (separately) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade; grade is mapped to approximate modal ages (9th=14, 10th=15, 11th=16, 12th=17). Missing estimates are set to 0 and flagged: pct_alcohol_drugs_before_sex_suppressed = 1 marks values CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample size), and pct_alcohol_drugs_before_sex_not_asked = 1 marks geography-years in which the question was not asked. Note: New York state estimates exclude New York City.

abcs_gas.name: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) Group A Streptococcus
abcs_gas.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
abcs_gas.description: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is a collaboration between CDC, state health departments and universities running active, population-based, laboratory-confirmed surveillance for invasive bacterial disease since 1997. CDC publishes one dataset per pathogen; this is the Group A Streptococcus. ABCs covers a catchment of selected US counties, roughly 35 million people, not the whole country. Rates are observed within that catchment and counts labelled national are CDC's population-weighted extrapolations. Values are national only, with no state or county breakdown. Invasive isolates are sent to CDC's reference laboratory and characterized by whole genome sequencing, which yields both the emm type and the predicted minimum inhibitory concentrations behind the resistance percentages. The published isolate counts start in 2006. Note CDC's own figures for 2023 disagree slightly: the surveillance report cites 3,908 isolates while the per-type counts in this dataset sum to 3,930, so the resistance and typing denominators are kept as separate columns here. A blank value is a cell CDC did not publish for that row, so a 0 is always a measured zero. CDC's case definition: invasive disease is isolation of group A Streptococcus from a normally sterile site, or from a wound culture accompanied by necrotizing fasciitis or streptococcal toxic shock syndrome, in a resident of a surveillance area.
abcs_gas.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

abcs_gbs.name: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) Group B Streptococcus
abcs_gbs.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
abcs_gbs.description: Active Bacterial Core surveillance (ABCs) is a collaboration between CDC, state health departments and universities running active, population-based, laboratory-confirmed surveillance for invasive bacterial disease since 1997. CDC publishes one dataset per pathogen; this is the Group B Streptococcus. ABCs covers a catchment of selected US counties, roughly 35 million people, not the whole country. Rates are observed within that catchment and counts labelled national are CDC's population-weighted extrapolations. Values are national only, with no state or county breakdown. Invasive isolates are characterized at CDC's reference laboratory. Serotype and ALPH percentages carry a per-population-group isolate count; the resistance percentages have a single overall count published from 2006 on, and none for the individual population groups. A blank value is a cell CDC did not publish for that row, so a 0 is always a measured zero. CDC's case definition: invasive disease is isolation of group B Streptococcus from a normally sterile site in a resident of a surveillance area.

cms_mmd.name: Mapping Medicare Disparities by Population Tool
cms_mmd.organization: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS)
cms_mmd.description: The Mapping Medicare Disparities (MMD) by Population Tool is an interactive map that displays chronic disease prevalence, costs, hospitalization, and preventive care utilization data for Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries. Data are available at the national, state, and county levels, stratified by age, race/ethnicity, and sex. Condition prevalence rates are calculated using ICD-10 diagnosis codes in Medicare claims data, following the Chronic Conditions Warehouse (CCW) definitions. The tool covers over 30 chronic conditions including diabetes, hypertension, COPD, heart failure, and mental health conditions, as well as preventive service utilization metrics. Data are updated annually.
cms_mmd.restrictions: Public domain. CMS data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

epic_cosmos.name: Epic Cosmos
epic_cosmos.description: Epic Cosmos is a collaborative research platform containing de-identified patient data from over 300 million patients across more than 1,600 hospitals and health systems using Epic electronic health record systems. Data is accessed via SlicerDicer, a self-service analytics tool. The dataset includes emergency department visits, diagnoses, immunizations, laboratory results, and other clinical data. Due to privacy protections, counts fewer than 10 are suppressed and imputed. Coverage extends across all U.S. states and territories. Note that county-level and city-level stratifications could differ markedly in total sample size due to high levels of missingness of county data in some states.
epic_cosmos.restrictions: The data can be re-used with appropriate attribution. A suggested citation relating to this data is 'Results of research performed with Epic Cosmos were obtained from the PopHIVE platform (https://github.com/PopHIVE/Ingest).'

nccr.name: National Childhood Cancer Registry Explorer (NCCR*Explorer)
nccr.organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), Childhood Cancer Data Initiative
nccr.location: NCCR*Explorer: An interactive website for NCCR cancer statistics
nccr.description: The National Childhood Cancer Registry (NCCR) is a federated data resource maintained by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) as part of the Childhood Cancer Data Initiative (CCDI). NCCR*Explorer provides precalculated incidence, survival, and prevalence statistics for cancers among children, adolescents, and young adults (ages 0-39) diagnosed from 2001 forward. Incidence data are pooled from up to 29 U.S. cancer registries representing approximately 76% of the U.S. population ages 0-39. Cancers are classified using the International Classification of Childhood Cancer (ICCC). Rates are age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population and reported at the national level only; NCCR*Explorer does not provide state- or registry-level breakdowns. Statistics are available by sex, race/ethnicity, and age group. This dataset was harvested from the NCCR*Explorer application data API (incidence, trends over time).
nccr.restrictions: Public domain. Data from the National Childhood Cancer Registry, produced by the National Cancer Institute, is generally not subject to copyright restrictions. Suggested attribution: National Childhood Cancer Registry Explorer (NCCR*Explorer), National Cancer Institute.

neiss.name: National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS)
neiss.location: NEISS public query / archived data files
neiss.description: NEISS is a national probability sample of hospital emergency departments (~100 of the ~5,000+ U.S. hospitals with 24-hour EDs) operated by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Each sampled record describes an injury treated in the ED, including patient age, sex, race, Hispanic ethnicity (added 2019), diagnosis, body part, disposition, up to three associated consumer products, and a statistical weight (plus sampling stratum and PSU). Sample weights scale records to national estimates; raw record counts are not nationally representative. This dataset covers treatment years from 2019 through the latest year CPSC has posted (auto-detected at ingest time), aggregated to national (geography='00') annual counts, in wide format: one neiss_n_ (raw sampled count) and one neiss_wt_ (weighted national estimate) column per primary-diagnosis or primary-product-group category. Product groups are reconstructed from NEISS product-code bands and are approximate, not an official CPSC taxonomy. Companion _rate files (data_*_rate.csv.gz) give injury rates per 100,000 population stratified by age and sex only, using the weighted estimate as numerator and a constant national age x sex population (mean of U.S. Census Vintage 2023 estimates, 2020-2023) as denominator.
neiss.restrictions: Public domain. NEISS data are produced by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and are generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nhtsa_fars.name: Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
nhtsa_fars.location: NHTSA File Downloads — FARS National CSV archives
nhtsa_fars.description: FARS is a nationwide census providing NHTSA, Congress, and the American public with yearly data on fatal injuries suffered in motor vehicle traffic crashes. FARS contains data on all crashes in the United States involving a fatality in a motor vehicle traffic crash on a public road. A fatal crash is one in which a motor vehicle is involved and at least one person dies within 30 days of the crash. Data are collected from police crash reports, state vehicle registration files, state driver licensing files, state highway department data, vital statistics, and other sources. FARS has been operational since 1975 and covers all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico (national files cover the 50 states and DC).
nhtsa_fars.restrictions: Public domain. NHTSA data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nis.name: National Immunization Survey-Teen (NIS-Teen)
nis.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nis.location: Vaccination Coverage among Adolescents (13-17 Years), TeenVaxView
nis.description: The National Immunization Surveys (NIS) are a group of telephone surveys used to monitor vaccination coverage among children 19-35 months, teens 13-17 years, flu vaccinations for children 6 months-17 years, and COVID-19 vaccination for children, teens, and adults. The surveys are sponsored and conducted by the National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases (NCIRD) of the CDC and authorized by the Public Health Service Act. NIS provides population-based, state and local area estimates of vaccination coverage using a standard survey methodology. Surveys collect data through telephone interviews with parents or guardians in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and some U.S. territories. Cell phone numbers are randomly selected and called to enroll age-eligible children. With parental permission, vaccination providers are contacted to verify immunization records. NIS-Teen covers adolescents aged 13-17 and reports coverage for HPV, Tdap, MenACWY, MMR, hepatitis A and B, and varicella by survey year for states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, plus pooled 2018-2022 estimates by insurance, poverty, race and ethnicity, and urbanicity. HHS regions and sub-state local areas published by CDC are not included here.
nis.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

wisqars.name: Web-based Injury Statistics Query and Reporting System (WISQARS)
wisqars.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
wisqars.description: WISQARS (Web-based Injury Statistics Query and Reporting System) is an interactive, online database that provides fatal and nonfatal injury, violent death, and cost of injury data from a variety of trusted sources. Maintained by CDC's National Center for Injury Prevention and Control, WISQARS enables public health professionals and researchers to access injury-related mortality data from the National Vital Statistics System, nonfatal injury data from the National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS), and violent death data from the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS). Data are available at national and state levels for various injury mechanisms including motor vehicle crashes, falls, poisonings (including drug overdoses), firearms, and self-harm. WISQARS supports injury surveillance, research, and prevention program planning.
wisqars.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

yrbss.name: CDC Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS)
yrbss.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
yrbss.description: The Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) is a set of school-based surveys conducted by the CDC that monitor health-related behaviors among U.S. high school students. The biennial national, state, and local surveys provide weighted prevalence estimates of behaviors contributing to the leading causes of death and disability. Data were accessed via the YRBS Explorer API. Estimates are provided overall and stratified (separately, not crossed) by sex, race/ethnicity, and grade. Estimates that CDC suppressed (e.g., small sample sizes) are omitted rather than imputed. State estimates are available only for jurisdictions that share data with CDC; Minnesota, Oregon, and Washington are not included, and New York state excludes New York City.
yrbss.restrictions: Public domain. Suggested attribution: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS).
